title: Two Mirrors Make a Rotation
eyebrow: Goosethropic Physics · Geometric Algebra · computed by garust via WebAssembly
lede: Reflect a vector across one mirror, then across another. What you get is a rotation — by twice the angle between the mirrors, no matter which vector you started with. Nothing on this page is animated by hand: every frame is garust computing sandwiches.

views.title: b (a v a) b = (b a) v (a b) = R v R̃

claims.text: Two reflections and one rotor sandwich land on the same vector.
The rotation is twice the mirror angle, whatever v was.
⟨R⟩₀ = cos Δ and the e₁₂ part is −sin Δ — pinned against garust, not assumed.
The same mirror twice is the identity.
The two constructions this page draws coincide at f64 scale.

tryThis: Drag the v slider: the rotation readout does not move — the rotor R = b a never heard of v.
Set both mirrors to the same angle: rotation 0.000 τ — reflecting twice across one mirror undoes itself.
Put the mirrors 0.25 τ apart: v comes back rotated half a turn, and ⟨R⟩₀ reads exactly 0 — the rotor is pure e₁₂.

card: The first GA-native lesson: every frame is garust computing sandwiches in 38 KB of WebAssembly. Reflections compose into a rotor; the angle doubles.
cardClaim: b (a v a) b = (b a) v (a b) — the rotor is the pair of reflections, reassociated.
